plan: [I account for winner’s curse. Unconditionally E[common value|signal=24]=24.5, but winning implies others had lower signals, lowering the conditional expectation. Using symmetry and the uniform noise/prior, E[common value | my signal=24 and I am highest] ≈ 23.82. In a second-price auction bidding that conditional expectation is near-optimal. I therefore shade my bid slightly below my signal to avoid the winner’s curse while remaining competitive.]

[Given S=37, prior C~Uniform(20,29) and noise N~Uniform(-20,20). Since 37−20=17 and 37+20=57, the feasible C is full [20,29], so posterior for C is uniform and E[C|S]=24.5. In a second-price auction, bid E[C|S] to avoid winner's curse and maximize expected profit.]

[My private signal is 10. Given the common value is uniform 20–29 and noise is uniform, the posterior expected common value is (20+29)/2 = 24.5. In a second-price auction with common-value signals, bidding E[common | signal] is the Bayes–Nash strategy that avoids the winner’s curse and maximizes expected surplus. Therefore I will bid $24.5 (valid to $0.1). This balances winning chances against overpaying.]
